interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 2, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Pound of Dale's ground beef" e "Pound of Liz's ground beef"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Sauce made by Dale."; "Sauce made by Liz."; "Both will have same amount of ground beef."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

erros.devolutiva: The denominator, the number below the fraction bar, determines how many equal parts the unit must have. Using 10 uses Dale’s numerator instead.

dicas.texto: Which part of a fraction tells how many equal pieces make one whole?
Look at the number below the fraction bar and use it to divide the interval from 0 to 1.
The number below the fraction bar determines the number of equal intervals.
Enter the denominator of Dale’s fraction in the division field, then confirm the division.
Compare the numerator with the denominator to decide whether the fraction reaches one whole.
Use the equal intervals on the first number line and count the required fractional parts from zero.
One whole is located at 9 ninths, so the target is the next ninth after that point.
Count nine equal intervals to reach one, then move one more ninth to mark Dale’s amount.
What does the denominator tell you about the number of equal parts?
Read Liz’s fraction and use the number below the fraction bar to divide one whole.
Liz’s denominator shows how many equal intervals are needed between 0 and 1.
Enter the denominator of Liz’s fraction in the second division field, then confirm it.
What location on a number line represents one complete whole?
Use Liz’s single equal interval and identify where the whole ends.
The target is the point where the first complete unit ends, between 0 and 2.
Place the marker at the endpoint of Liz’s one whole and confirm the point.
On a number line, which position represents the ... amount: the one farther right or the one farther left?
Compare each marked point with the location of one whole.
Dale’s numerator is one more than the number of parts in one whole.
Determine whether Dale’s point is to the right or left of Liz’s point, then select the matching comparison.
Which sauce is represented by the point farther to the right on the number line?
Use the comparison from the marked positions to choose the sauce with the larger amount.
One marked amount is exactly one whole, while the other is slightly beyond one whole.
Choose the sauce connected to the point beyond one whole, then press Done to submit.

exercicio.statement:
Dale and Liz are each making their own spaghetti sauce, and are using different amounts of ground beef to make it. If you wanted your sauce to have more ground beef, whose sauce should you choose? Use the number line to find out.
Dale is using 10/9 pounds of ground beef.
Liz is using exactly 1 pound of ground beef.
Which sauce should you choose?
